summary: Keyflower blends tile auctions with worker placement across four seasonal rounds, where colored workers both bid for new village tiles and activate abilities on any tile at the table — including opponents'. It rewards reading the auction carefully and squeezing value from other players' villages as much as building up your own.
praised: brilliant mechanism of activating others' tiles
strong tension in the winter round when workers can't leave
high replayability from modular tile setup
scales well to higher player counts
criticised: fiddly bookkeeping with many worker colors and tile abilities
upkeep tracking who benefits from which tile action

interaction.detail: Players bid workers against each other for new tiles, and crucially any player's workers can activate abilities on any other player's village tiles, making much of the board a shared resource that everyone actively exploits rather than private territory.

scoring.why: Points come from tile abilities, resources, skills, and bonus tiles accumulated across four rounds.
scoring.how_you_win: Win key tile auctions to assemble an efficient village while also exploiting both your own and opponents' tiles for resources and points.
